page: Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is a general-purpose, low-memory virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The instance configuration exposes 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The compute architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by x86_64 instruction sets including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic hardware acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory is configured at 8.0 GB, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (2.0 GB per core). This lower memory allocation differentiates the instance from standard 1:4 general-purpose tiers. The VM includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and requires network-attached storage, although it supports Azure Premium Storage. There are no hardware GPUs or included complimentary public IPv4 addresses with this configuration.

Performance benchmarks reflect strong single-threaded CPU capabilities, scoring within the top 25% in both stress-ng single-core tests and Geekbench 6 single-core evaluations. Multi-threaded processing and general computation align with mid-tier expectations, as observed in stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics. Conversely, memory subsystem benchmarks demonstrate lower throughput, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10% and large-block uncached read bandwidth measuring 36.9 GB/sec. Large model inference tasks, such as 7B parameter LLM processing, show constrained execution rates due to the restricted RAM capacity.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the D4als_v6 stems from its reduced memory density, allowing compute-focused operations that do not require extensive RAM pools to avoid paying for unneeded memory capacity. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web servers, reverse proxies, CI/CD runners, text processing jobs, and microservices that prioritize clock speed and modern vector instructions over memory-heavy caches or large local datasets.
description: Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, running on a dedicated 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture with 2 physical multithreaded cores, the instance includes AVX-512 extensions and dedicated cryptographic instruction sets. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it functions as a low-memory variant without included local disk storage, relying on external Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, balanced multi-core output, but weak memory subsystem bandwidth and constrained medium-scale LLM processing. Operating without attached GPUs, the D4als_v6 offers an efficient resource balance for workloads requiring compute capacity without massive RAM overhead, including static web serving, software utilities, text parsing, and lightweight microservices.
